title: EU AI Act Article 43: Conformity Assessment — The Gate Before the CE Mark
context: 2026-08-29 engine cycle — answer-first seed for EU AI Act Article 43 conformity assessment procedures; high-risk AI systems must complete a conformity assessment before CE marking and market placement, and the assessment path chosen (internal control vs notified body) determines speed-to-market and audit depth
body: Article 43 of the EU AI Act is the procedural gate every high-risk AI system must pass before it gets a CE mark and enters the European market. It is not a technical specification — it is the legal pathway that chooses which technical checks matter. The Act offers three routes: (1) internal control based on Annex VI, where the provider self-assesses against the harmonised standards and draws up a written declaration of conformity — this is the fast track and applies when the provider can demonstrate full compliance with harmonised standards or common specifications; (2) notified body assessment under Annex VII, where an independent third party audits the quality management system and the technical documentation — required when harmonised standards are not fully applied or for certain Annex III high-risk categories; and (3) the EU-type examination certificate route, the deepest review, where the notified body examines the actual AI system design. The choice of route matters enormously for an AI attestation provider: if a provider has a robust quality management system (Article 17) and technical documentation (Article 11) that maps cleanly to harmonised standards, it can use the internal-control route and self-declare conformity, which is faster and cheaper but places the entire credibility burden on the provider. The Council of AI treats conformity assessment as the same class of problem as containment: monitored containment, not provable isolation. A self-declared conformity assessment plus an independent signature over the declaration does not prove the AI system is safe — it proves the safety claim is attributable, well-structured, and verifiable, which is the honest, audit-grade guarantee that a notified body or a procurer actually needs. For a UK-based provider selling into the EU, Article 43 is the single most important article to instrument, because the conformity route determines whether a UK AISI-tested system can use UK test evidence as part of an EU conformity declaration, or whether a separate EU notified body re-assessment is required.
